summary: One role cleared every hard gate on October 20: Langfuse’s Senior Software Engineer, SDK, now part of ClickHouse. It publishes a €90,000–€160,000 annual salary with equity and names France among six remote-first European countries, with Berlin visits of 3–5 days every two months. The role owns the open-source Python and TypeScript SDKs that trace and evaluate LLM applications and agents. Six other roles were examined: three near-misses (Langfuse Senior Product Engineer, Mistral AI Evaluation Engineer and White Circle AI Red Team Engineer) and three rejections for non-AI-central, management or on-site remits. These entries are research leads, not recommendations.
coverage: Automated official-ATS sweep on October 20: 128 of 274 attempted Ashby, Lever and Greenhouse board aliases returned data; many failed aliases are likely wrong board names, not evidence of no vacancies. AI-titled roles on reachable boards were screened, as was every Paris- or France-located engineering role with published pay on reachable Ashby boards (92 roles). Three web searches were used for discovery through a fallback search provider; automated page extraction was unavailable, so pages were read through official ATS APIs and browser rendering. Seven roles were examined individually and seven application forms rendered. Coverage is bounded, not exhaustive.
criteria: Paris hybrid with explicit attendance, or fully remote explicitly allowing France-based applicants.
Senior/staff hands-on AI-central engineering; an AI employer, coding assistant use or AI product UI alone does not establish the required assignment.

Employer-published annual gross cash-base lower bound strictly above €100,000, or at least €80,000 with explicit equity. Use the lower bound; equity is not cash; packages, OTE and estimates do not pass.
No unchanged prior selections. Requisition identity takes precedence over refreshed titles, URLs or timestamps; historical qualification is not current-live verification.
uncertainty: Sources checked October 20, 2026. Posting dates come from employer ATS metadata.

Langfuse’s ATS labels its roles “Hybrid” without a city; remote eligibility from France rests on the six named countries plus the company careers page describing European roles as remote-first with periodic Berlin visits. The careers page is company-wide, not role-specific.
Langfuse publishes one €90,000–€160,000 range across six countries; the listing says actual pay may be higher or lower. A France-specific offer is not verified, and equity terms are unquantified.
Unpublished pay is recorded as unknown, not as below the threshold. Anthropic’s and Dust’s published figures are not confirmed as cash base (OTE or “Full Comp” wording).

Deduplication covered the accessible October 10–19 reports and the supplied October 3/5 Escape history. None of today’s requisition IDs appear in those reports. The Langfuse Product and Backend roles were posted on September 18 but were missed by earlier title-based screens; they are new to this site’s history, not newly created.
Company financial figures are company-reported or press-reported, not audited. Langfuse revenue, profitability, runway and headcount are not publicly verified.
decision: No approval needed for this authorized daily website update. One role qualified today: Langfuse’s Senior Software Engineer, SDK. Before applying, readers should confirm the France pay band and the Berlin travel cadence with the employer. Near-misses need published pay or explicit eligibility before reconsideration. No applications or outreach were made.

jobs.title: Langfuse - Senior Software Engineer, SDK
jobs.locationQuote: Location: Germany; France; Italy; Portugal; Spain; The Netherlands. ATS location type: Hybrid. Langfuse careers page: “European roles are remote-first with 3-5 days every two months in Berlin (travel covered); SF and Berlin locals use the office when it's useful.”[1][3]

salary.quote: “Salary €90K – €160K • Offers Equity”; the official ATS data classifies the €90,000–€160,000 component as an annual EUR salary. The listing adds that every new team member receives stock options. One published range covers all six listed countries.[1]

reasons: Pay passes the €80,000-plus-equity branch: the published annual salary floor is €90,000 and equity is explicitly offered. Equity is not counted as cash, and the €90,000 floor alone does not clear the €100,000 cash-only branch.[1]

Location passes: France is one of six named countries, and Langfuse states that European roles are remote-first. The role still requires 3–5 days in Berlin every two months, with travel covered, and the ATS labels it “Hybrid”.[1][3]

AI centrality passes: the role owns Python and TypeScript SDKs that instrument LLM applications and agent loops, maintains integrations with 40+ AI frameworks and model providers, and supports evaluation workflows such as the experiment runner. The craft is SDK and API engineering rather than model training.[1][4]
Seniority is explicit in the title. It was first published on October 19, 2026, and the same-page application form rendered on the check date.[1][2]
jobs.product: Langfuse is an open-source (MIT) LLM engineering platform for tracing, evaluation and prompt management, used by teams building AI applications and agents. Its SDKs are built on OpenTelemetry, so third-party instrumentations appear inside Langfuse traces, and they also expose the prompt-management and evaluation features.[4] This role owns those SDKs: reliability and low CPU and memory overhead inside customers’ production systems, from serverless functions to long-running agent loops; batching, async flushing and graceful degradation; framework integrations; the OTLP endpoint; and contributing to OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions.[1] A concrete near-term problem is migration: Langfuse’s docs say the legacy POST /api/public/ingestion endpoint on Langfuse Cloud stops accepting everything except scores on November 16, 2026.[4] A narrower assigned project beyond SDK ownership is unknown.
jobs.financials: Langfuse was acquired by ClickHouse, announced on January 16, 2026, alongside ClickHouse’s $400 million Series D led by Dragoneer; the acquisition price was not disclosed.[5] TechCrunch, citing Bloomberg, reported a $15 billion valuation for that round.[7] ClickHouse reported more than 3,000 ClickHouse Cloud customers and ARR growth above 250% year over year; these are company claims, not audited financial statements.[5] Langfuse said it had term sheets for a Series A before choosing the acquisition and that it remains open source and self-hostable.[6] Langfuse ended 2025 with over 20K GitHub stars and 26M+ SDK installs per month, per ClickHouse.[5] Revenue, profitability, runway and Langfuse team headcount are not publicly verified.
